questions.question: Which is one role of play in the pre-school and early childhood years?

choices.C: Increases imagination due to expanding knowledge and emotional range.
choices.D: Develops the upper and lower limbs.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Early childhood play is primarily cooperative or associative rather than focused on structured competition[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Play often blurs the line between fantasy and reality through pretend play rather than separating them cleanly[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Correct. Play allows young children to explore roles, expand cognitive symbolism, and broaden their emotional and imaginative capacities[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Physical motor development is a benefit, but play holistically integrates cognitive and emotional growth beyond just limb development[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Play serves as a primary vehicle for cognitive, social, and emotional growth in early childhood, fostering creative symbolism and expanding imaginative boundaries[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: EARLY PLAY = EXPANDS IMAGINATION & emotional range[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Child and Adolescent Development — Play in Early Childhood[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Development

questions.question: Student Z does not study at all but when the Licensure Examination for Teachers (LET) comes, before he takes the LET, he spends one hour or more praying for a miracle, i.e. to pass the exam. Which attitude towards religion or God is displayed?

rationalization.A: Incorrect. The student genuinely believes praying will alter the outcome, showing reliance rather than viewing it as fake[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Treating religion as 'magic' involves attempting to manipulate divine intervention for personal shortcuts without putting in required effort[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Authentic religion integrates faith with personal responsibility and moral action ('Nasa Diyos ang awa, nasa tao ang gawa')[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. 'Religion as real' does not capture the distorted transactional expectation of instant miracles without effort[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Viewing religion as magic treats prayer as a superstitious shortcut to achieve results without fulfilling personal duties or preparation[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: PRAYER WITHOUT EFFORT = RELIGION AS MAGIC[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Sociology of Education — Religious Attitudes & Values[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: As a teacher, you are a rationalist. Which among these will be your guiding principle?

choices.A: I must teach the child that we can never have real knowledge of anything.
choices.B: I must teach the child to develop his mental powers to the full.
choices.C: I must teach the child so he is assured of heaven.
choices.D: I must teach the child every knowledge, skill, and value that he needs for a better future.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Claiming we can never have real knowledge reflects Skepticism or Agnosticism[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Rationalism asserts that reason and mental intellect are the primary sources of truth and knowledge, requiring full development of mental powers[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Teaching for assurance of heaven reflects Scholasticism or Religious Idealism[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Teaching everything needed for a practical future aligns with Pragmatism or Utilitarianism[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Rationalism holds that reason and logical thinking are the chief sources of knowledge, prioritizing the development of the mind's cognitive faculties[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: All men are pretty much alike. It is only by custom that they are set apart, said one Oriental philosopher. Where can this thought be most inspiring?

choices.A: In a multi-cultural group of learners
choices.B: In multi-cultural and heterogeneous groups of learners and indigenous peoples' group
choices.C: In a class composed of indigenous peoples

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Narrower than option B, which explicitly encompasses both multicultural classrooms and indigenous communities[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Confucius' insight emphasizes universal human unity over superficial cultural differences, serving as a powerful inclusive principle in diverse classrooms[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Homogeneous indigenous classes lack the intercultural contrast where custom sets people apart[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Omits the specific multicultural and indigenous context emphasized in inclusive pedagogy[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Confucius' statement highlights that underlying human nature is shared, while cultural customs create perceived differences; this fosters empathy in diverse learning environments[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: ALL MEN ALIKE = UNIVERSAL HUMAN INCLUSION in diverse groups[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Foundations of Education — Multicultural & Inclusive Education[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: Teacher A discovered that his pupils are very good in dramatizing. Which tool must have helped him discover his pupils' strength?

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Portfolios compile accumulated artifacts over time rather than evaluating live dramatic performance directly[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Performance tests evaluate active, hands-on demonstrations and behavioral execution, such as acting or dramatization[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Journal entries measure reflective written expression[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Paper-and-pencil tests evaluate cognitive recall and written knowledge, not dramatic skill[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Performance-based assessment measures students' ability to execute specific motor, artistic, or behavioral tasks in real-time[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Assessment of Learning

questions.question: NSAT and NEAT results are interpreted against set mastery level. This means that NSAT and NEAT fall under __________.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Intelligence tests evaluate general cognitive capacity (IQ)[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Aptitude tests predict future learning potential in specific fields[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Correct. Criterion-referenced testing evaluates student performance against an absolute, pre-determined standard or mastery percentage[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Norm-referenced testing compares an individual's score relative to peer group percentiles[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Interpreting test scores against a fixed benchmark or 'set mastery level' defines criterion-referenced evaluation[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Assessment of Learning — Test Interpretation Frameworks[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Assessment of Learning

questions.question: In a social studies class, Teacher I presents a morally ambiguous situation and asks his students what they would do. On whose theory is Teacher I's technique based?

rationalization.A: Correct. Lawrence Kohlberg used moral dilemmas (ambiguous ethical situations) to evaluate stages of moral reasoning[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Preserved source key lists B (Bandura), though Bandura focused on observational modeling rather than moral dilemma discussions[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Piaget studied cognitive development and early moral judgment stages, but Kohlberg perfected the dilemma technique[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Bruner developed discovery learning and representation modes[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Kohlberg used moral dilemmas to examine stages of moral reasoning; Bandura is associated with observational learning and social cognitive theory.
questions.reference: Child and Adolescent Development — Kohlberg's Moral Development[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Development
questions.dataNote: CORRECT KEY: A moral dilemma technique is associated with Kohlberg, not Bandura.

questions.question: Which is a sound classroom management practice?

choices.B: Establish routines for all daily needs and tasks.
choices.C: Apply rules and policies on a case to case basis.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Avoiding routines leads to chaos and wasted instructional time[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Establishing predictable routines for daily tasks minimizes confusion, saves time, and prevents behavioral disruptions[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Inconsistent application of rules creates confusion and perceptions of unfairness[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Reactive discipline addresses problems after they occur; proactive discipline is preferred[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Clear, well-rehearsed classroom routines establish order, maximize academic learning time, and reduce misbehavior[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Classroom Management

questions.question: A sixth grade twelve-year old boy comes from a dysfunctional family and has been abused and neglected. He has been to two orphanages and three different elementary schools. The student can decide on the second grade level, but he can comprehend orally material at the fourth or fifth grade level. The most probable cause/s of this student's reading problem is/are __________.

rationalization.A: Correct. Trauma, severe neglect, abuse, and family instability create severe emotional distress that blocks decoding and reading development despite normal oral comprehension[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Multiple school changes contributed, but emotional trauma from abuse is the primary root cause described[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Preserved source key lists C, though the scenario emphasizes severe socio-emotional trauma rather than organic brain damage[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Chronologically 12 years old, so age immaturity is not the cause[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Severe abuse, neglect, family instability, and repeated school changes can create emotional and adjustment difficulties that interfere with academic performance. The item does not provide evidence of neurological damage.
questions.reference: Special Education — Factors Affecting Reading Performance[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Special Education
questions.dataNote: CORRECT KEY: The scenario strongly emphasizes abuse, neglect, family instability, and school disruption; the dataset's own rationalization identifies emotional factors.

questions.question: Teacher U teaches to his pupils that pleasure is not the highest good. Teacher's teaching is against what philosophy?

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Realism posits that physical matter and objective reality exist independently of perception[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Hedonism claims that pleasure is the ultimate intrinsic good and primary goal of human life; teaching against pleasure as highest good opposes Hedonism[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Epicureanism advocates refined pleasure through tranquility and absence of pain, but Hedonism is the primary umbrella philosophy[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Empiricism asserts that knowledge originates in sensory experience[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Hedonism evaluates morality based on pleasure optimization. Denying that pleasure is the supreme good opposes hedonistic tenets[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: With which goals of educational institutions as provided for by the Constitution is the development of work skills aligned?

choices.B: To teach the duties of citizenship

rationalization.B: Incorrect. Relates to civic obligations and public service[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Relates to patriotism and national pride[cite: 12].

questions.question: Direct instruction is for facts, rules, and actions as indirect instruction is for __________, __________, __________.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Describes steps in scientific inquiry[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Missing higher-order conceptual generalizations[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Correct. Direct instruction explicitly teaches step-by-step facts and rules, whereas indirect instruction engages learners in discovering concepts, processes, and generalizations[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Informal vocabulary[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Indirect instruction is student-centered and inquiry-based, guiding learners to discover overarching concepts, cognitive processes, and broad generalizations[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: DIRECT = Facts & Rules; INDIRECT = Concepts, Processes, Generalizations[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Principles of Teaching — Direct vs Indirect Instruction[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Principles of Teaching

questions.question: To elicit more student's response, Teacher G made use of covert responses. Which one did she NOT do?

choices.A: She had the students write their response privately.
choices.B: She showed the correct answers on the overhead after the students have written their responses.
choices.C: She had the students write their responses privately then called each of them.
choices.D: She refrained from judging on the student's responses.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Writing responses privately is a covert (internal/private) response strategy[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Displaying correct answers for self-checking maintains private, covert reflection[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Correct. Calling on each student to state their private response publicly transforms the private covert response into an overt (publicly observable) response[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Refraining from immediate judgment encourages covert thinking[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Covert responses are private or internal. Having students write privately is covert; calling each student to state the response aloud makes it overt.
questions.reference: Principles of Teaching — Active Response Strategies[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Principles of Teaching
questions.dataNote: CORRECT KEY: Calling students to state their responses publicly converts a covert/private response into an overt response.

questions.question: What should you do if a parent who is concerned about a grade his child received compared to another student's grade, demands to see both students' grades?

choices.C: Refuse to show any record without expressing permission from principal.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Parents have a legal right to inspect their own child's academic records[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Preserved source key lists B, but disclosing another student's grades violates student privacy laws (Family Educational Rights and Privacy / Data Privacy Act)[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. A teacher can show a parent their own child's grade without special principal permission[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Correct. Confidentiality regulations allow parents to inspect only their own child's academic records[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Student records are confidential. The teacher should show only the requesting parent's own child's record and protect the other student's privacy.
questions.memoryTip: PARENT ASKS FOR GRADES = SHOW ONLY THEIR CHILD'S RECORD
questions.reference: The Teaching Profession — Code of Ethics & Privacy Laws[cite: 12]
questions.subject: The Teaching Profession
questions.dataNote: CORRECT KEY: A parent may access the child's own educational record but should not be shown another student's grades.

questions.question: John Watson said: Men are built not born. What does this statement point to?

choices.A: The ineffectiveness of training on a person's development.
choices.B: The effect of environmental stimulation on a person's development.
choices.C: The absence of genetic influence on a person's development

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Watson asserted training and environment are completely effective in shaping humans[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. John B. Watson, founder of Behaviorism, asserted that environmental conditioning and nurture shape human development ('built') rather than innate heredity ('born')[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. While Watson minimized heredity, the statement positively emphasizes environmental influence[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. 'Born' refers to heredity, which Watson rejected[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Behaviorism posits that environmental conditioning and learning experiences ('nurture') construct human behavior[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: MEN ARE BUILT NOT BORN = BEHAVIORISM / Environmental influence[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Child and Adolescent Development — Behavioral Theories[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Child and Adolescent Development

questions.question: A guest speaker at a graduation ceremony told his audience: "You are what you choose to be." The guest speaker is more of a/an __________.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Realism emphasizes physical matter and objective reality[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Pragmatism emphasizes practical consequences and active testing[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Idealism emphasizes eternal ideas and spiritual mind[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Correct. Existentialism centers on individual choice, free will, and personal responsibility ('you are what you choose to be')[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Existentialist philosophy asserts that existence precedes essence, meaning humans define their identity through free choices[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: YOU ARE WHAT YOU CHOOSE = EXISTENTIALISM[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: The best way for a guidance counselor to begin to develop study skills and habits in underachieving student would be to __________.

choices.A: have these underachieving students observe the study habits of excelling students
choices.B: encourage students to talk about study habits from their own experiences
choices.C: have them view film strips about various study approaches
choices.D: give out a list of effective study approaches

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Passive observation may intimidate underachievers[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. Starting from students' personal experiences establishes rapport, self-awareness, and active reflection on current study difficulties[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Viewing films is passive and non-interactive[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Handing out lists without discussion lacks personal engagement[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Guidance counseling begins with reflective dialogue, encouraging students to self-examine current habits before introducing new techniques[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: COUNSELING FIRST STEP = Reflected dialogue on OWN EXPERIENCES[cite: 12].
questions.reference: Guidance and Counseling — Study Skills Intervention[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: Principal C shares this thought with his teachers: Subject matter should help students understand and appreciate themselves as unique individuals who accept complete responsibility for their thoughts, feelings, and actions. From which philosophy is this thought based?

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Perennialism focuses on universal truths and classical literature[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Essentialism focuses on core academic subjects and teacher authority[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Correct. Existentialism highlights individual uniqueness, self-knowledge, free choice, and personal responsibility for one's life[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Progressivism focuses on democratic problem-solving and social experience[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Existentialist education helps learners explore individual identity, personal freedom, and personal accountability[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Foundations of Education

questions.question: The search for related literature by accessing several databases by the use of a telephone line to connect a computer library with other computers that have database is termed __________.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. CD-ROM searches access local optical discs[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Manual searching uses physical card catalogs or printed indexes[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Correct. Telecommunication connections linking computers to remote online databases constitute an on-line search[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Too generic, as local offline computer searches do not require telecommunication lines[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Online searching uses telecommunication networks to access external digital databases and electronic libraries[cite: 12].
questions.memoryTip: CONNECTING TO REMOTE DATABASES = ON-LINE SEARCH[cite: 12].
questions.subject: Educational Technology

questions.question: Teacher W wants to review and check on the lesson of the previous day? Which one will be most reliable?

choices.A: Having students identify difficult homework problems.
choices.B: Having students correct each other's work.
choices.C: Sampling the understanding of a few students.
choices.D: Explicitly reviewing the task-relevant information necessary for the day's lesson.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Only highlights confusing areas rather than systematically reinforcing core concepts[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Peer correction checks compliance but does not ensure whole-class instructional review[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Preserved source key lists C, but sampling a few students is unreliable as it misses overall class understanding[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Correct. Direct instruction models advocate explicitly reviewing key prerequisite information to ensure a solid foundation for the new lesson[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Explicitly reviewing prerequisite, task-relevant information checks the knowledge needed for the next lesson more systematically than sampling only a few students.
questions.reference: Principles of Teaching — Direct Instruction Model[cite: 12]
questions.subject: Principles of Teaching
questions.dataNote: CORRECT KEY: The most systematic review is explicit review of task-relevant prerequisite information for the day's lesson.

rationalization.D: Incorrect. Discovery learning is an indirect strategy[cite: 12].

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Problem-centered learning revolves around solving real-world cases[cite: 12].

rationalization.C: Incorrect. Focuses on literacy integration[cite: 12].

questions.question: Read the following then answer the question Teacher: In what ways other than the periodic table might we predict the undiscovered elements? Bobby: We could go to the moon and see if there are some elements there we don't have. Betty: We could dig down into the center of the earth and see if we find any of the missing elements. Ricky: We could study debris from the meteorites if we can find any. Teacher: Those are all good answers. but what if those excursions to the moon, to the center of the earth, or to find meteorites were too costly and time consuming? how might we use the elements we already have here on earth to find some new ones? Question: The Teacher's questions in the above exchange are examples of __________ questions.

rationalization.A: Incorrect. Fact questions require simple recall[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Correct. The teacher asks conceptual/divergent questions that prompt students to apply underlying scientific principles rather than reciting memorized facts[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Preserved source key lists C, though the exchange demonstrates conceptual/divergent questioning[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Closed questions have single fixed answers[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: The teacher asks learners to think beyond recall and generate possible explanations or approaches. These are conceptual, open-ended questions rather than closed factual questions.
questions.subject: Principles of Teaching
questions.dataNote: RETAIN/CLEAN: The exchange is best classified as conceptual/open-ended questioning; the original key C (direct) conflicts with the question type.

questions.question: In his second item analysis, Teacher H found out that more from the lower group got the test item # 6 correctly. This means that the test item __________.

rationalization.A: Correct. When more low-performing students answer an item correctly than high-performing students, the item has negative discrimination and should be revised or rejected[cite: 12].
rationalization.B: Incorrect. Preserved source key lists B, but item analysis specifically evaluates the Discrimination Index[cite: 12].
rationalization.C: Incorrect. Positive discrimination means more upper-group students passed the item[cite: 12].
rationalization.D: Incorrect. Reliability measures test consistency[cite: 12].

questions.explanation: Negative discrimination occurs when the lower-performing group outperforms the upper-performing group on an item, signaling a potentially flawed item.
questions.memoryTip: LOWER GROUP > UPPER GROUP = NEGATIVE DISCRIMINATION
questions.subject: Assessment of Learning
questions.dataNote: CORRECT KEY: When more lower-group students answer an item correctly than upper-group students, the item has negative discrimination.

questions.question: The design of the 2002 Basic Education Curriculum (BEC) is based on the principles that the main sources for contemporary basic education are the expert systems of knowledge and the learner's experience in their context. questions.explanation: Combining expert discipline knowledge (Essentialism) with contextualized learner experience (Constructivism) balances subject rigor with active learning[cite: 12].
